sentences.text: The type specimen of Jianchangosaurus was a juvenile discovered in Jianchang County, western Liaoning Province.
This holotype is an almost complete skeleton of a single juvenile individual, lacking only the distal part of the tail.
Despite being a basal therizinosaur, Jianchangosaurus possessed key anatomical features like a beaked premaxilla and a specific pubic boot shape.
The premaxilla and the front portion of the maxilla lacked teeth, while small foramina on the premaxilla suggest that Jianchangosaurus had a beak.
The skull of Jianchangosaurus measures 230 millimeters in length and is 10% longer than the femur.
Jianchangosaurus possesses 27 maxillary teeth and approximately 25 to 25 dentary teeth.
The crowns of Jianchangosaurus teeth decrease in size as they progress toward the back of the skull.
Jianchangosaurus possessed barely curved hand claws with weak flexor tubercles positioned ventrally relative to the articular face.
The preserved skeleton includes ten cervical vertebrae ranging from the atlas to the last neck bone, all of which are amphicoelous and highly pneumatized.
Jianchangosaurus is estimated to have stood one meter high at the hips and measured approximately two meters in length.
Wide and unbranched feather impressions surround the holotype of Jianchangosaurus, with only their distal ends visible.
Researchers speculated that the wide and unbranched feathers of Jianchangosaurus may have been used for visual display.
The presence of wide, elongated filamentous feathers suggests they may have been used for display.
Fossil remains, an almost complete juvenile specimen missing the distal tail, were found in the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, northeast China.
Jianchangosaurus was described and named by Hanyong Pu, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Junchang Lu, Li Xu, Yanhua Wu, Huali Chang, Jiming Zhang, and Songhai Jia in 2013.
The genus name Jianchangosaurus is derived from the discovery county and the Greek word for lizard.
Jianchangosaurus's dental morphology likely maximized biting stress to help it effectively slice plant fibers.
In 2013, Pu et al. noted that the dental morphology likely maximized bite stress to cut plant fibers, similar to ornithopods and ceratopsians.
The lower jaw was rotated downward to work with the upper rhamphotheca for stripping food.
Derived skull features suggest adaptations for feeding on plant material.
Jianchangosaurus is classified as a basal therizinosaur, similar to the primitive genera Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus.
Jianchangosaurus was classified as a basal therizinosaur, similar to Falcarius utahensis and Beipiaosaurus inexpectus.
Jianchangosaurus is the only known therizinosaur with tail vertebrae that are oval in shape.
Jianchangosaurus yixianensis is the only known therizinosaur with a tail featuring caudal centra that are oval in shape.
Jianchangosaurus lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 126 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Jianchangosaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
The validity of Jianchangosaurus is debated, with Cau (2024) arguing it is a junior synonym of Beipiaosaurus because distinguishing features are based on ontogenetically variable characters.

Liao and colleagues (2026) supported the distinction of Jianchangosaurus from Beipiaosaurus, suggesting the former was better adapted for running while the latter had a more robust, less cursorial morphology.
